destination.title: Inflation and accelerated cosmology: mechanisms and tests
destination.question: How do specified gravitational, scalar, kinetic and dissipative constructions realize inflation and related cosmological phases, and what can their dynamical, observational, geometric and conditional quantum-gravity tests establish?
destination.summary: Organize by physical target, framework and regime across batches. Model construction, inflationary evolution, quantum initial states, late acceleration and consistency diagnostics remain distinguishable. Classical nonsingular cosmology and research-resource questions retain comparison routes. The parent scope is a new proposal requiring independent review.

systems: Source-specific gravitational, scalar, kinetic and dissipative cosmological models
Supergravity, microscopic constructions and effective descriptions with distinct completion claims
De Sitter field and horizon systems
Adjacent classical nonsingular, compact-object consistency and research-resource settings
targets: Inflationary construction, background evolution, control and primordial predictions
Initial conditions, transitions, exit and postinflationary outputs
Late acceleration and explicitly proposed early-to-late connections
Conditional conjecture compatibility, field geometry and effective-theory validity
Boundary comparisons involving information capacity and research tools
regimes: Slow roll, constant roll and rapid turn only where specified
Cold, warm and dissipative evolution as distinct cases
High-energy brane calculations within their stated density limit
Quantum initial-state and stochastic self-reproduction questions kept separate
Inflationary, postinflationary, late-time and classical nonsingular phases distinguished
assumptions: Every construction retains its own action, fields, dimensions and validity conditions
Conjectures are conditional diagnostics, not universal premises or sufficient conditions for ultraviolet completion
Numerical batches supply provenance rather than mandatory public branches
Descendant coverage is attributed to the supplied child ledgers, not reconstructed from the contrast rows
conventions: Preserve source-specific frames, normalizations, derivatives, conjecture versions and observational dates
Distinguish background dynamics, potential diagnostics, perturbative control and empirical comparisons
Treat source-object relations as typed context rather than independently established physical premises
includes: Negative findings, open constructions and unresolved applicability
Compound source questions with multiple typed contributions
Contextual alternatives outside the physical inflation core
excludes: A universal viability, exclusion or ultraviolet-completion claim
Canonical question equivalence inferred from numerical ancestry
Treating publication growth or AI performance as constraints on inflationary potentials

sources.title: The Standard Model Higgs boson as the inflaton

evidence.text: Can the Standard Model Higgs drive inflation and generate acceptable primordial perturbations through a non-minimal gravitational coupling, without introducing an additional inflaton particle?

sources.title: Disentangling the $f(R)$ - Duality

evidence.text: How do decaying exponentials, rising exponentials, and monomial deformations of inflationary plateaus change their f(R) descriptions, including asymptotic powers, closed-form reconstructibility, and observable inflationary behavior?

sources.title: Gauss-Bonnet Inflation

evidence.text: Can a scalar coupled to the Gauss–Bonnet invariant generate early de Sitter expansion and an exit without an imposed scalar self-potential, after neglecting the Einstein–Hilbert term in a proposed strong-gravity regime?

sources.title: Warm inflation within a supersymmetric distributed mass model

evidence.text: Which mass distributions in a supersymmetric distributed mass model permit controlled warm inflation with a quartic potential, observational agreement, and compatibility with the proposed swampland criteria?

sources.title: $\alpha$-attractor from superconformal E-models in brane inflation

evidence.text: Do superconformal E-model potentials retain inflationary attractors in Randall–Sundrum II brane cosmology, and how do brane corrections affect ns, r, parameter degeneracies and sub-Planckian field excursions?

sources.title: A note on supergravity inflation in braneworld

evidence.text: Can supergravity-motivated power-law potentials with exponential suppression yield observationally compatible inflation and sub-Planckian field excursions when embedded phenomenologically in braneworld cosmology?

sources.title: Multi-field Inflation in High-Slope Potentials

evidence.text: Can strongly turning multi-field trajectories support prolonged, observationally compatible inflation on steep potentials while satisfying the refined de Sitter and distance swampland criteria, in flat or negatively curved field space?

sources.title: Logarithmic corrected $f(R)$ gravitational model and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Determine whether corrected f(R) inflation can accommodate the paper's conjectured quantum-gravity restrictions and reported cosmological information, and whether those requirements constrain the curvature exponent and correction coefficients.

sources.title: Warm tachyon inflation and swampland criteria

evidence.text: Determine whether observational compatibility survives checks of thermal dominance and strong dissipation, and whether the resulting tachyon trajectories satisfy the paper's two proposed swampland inequalities.

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: The setting describes inflation driven by one canonical scalar coupled to the Gauss–Bonnet invariant. This interaction changes homogeneous evolution and cosmological perturbation propagation and normalization.

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: Can a corresponding luminality-constrained Swampland analysis be developed for string cosmology with two scalar fields?

sources.title: Swampland Constraints on No-Boundary Quantum Cosmology

evidence.text: Can the traditional Hartle–Hawking state give appreciable relative weight to classical inflationary universes when Einstein gravity with a scalar field obeys the assumed distance and refined de Sitter conjectures?

sources.title: CMB from a Gauss-Bonnet-induced de Sitter fixed point

evidence.text: Can de Sitter fixed points sustained by a balance between a massive scalar potential and a scalar-dependent Gauss-Bonnet coupling generate CMB-compatible fluctuations, and thereby constrain the coupling function?

sources.title: Rapid-turn inflation in supergravity is rare and tachyonic

evidence.text: How readily can sustained rapid-turn inflation arise in supergravity, and what do its turning rate, field-space curvature and Hessian spectrum imply for the multifield η-problem and de Sitter swampland conjecture?

sources.title: Cosmic inflation from broken conformal symmetry

evidence.text: Can an asymptotically flat inflationary potential emerge from Palatini quadratic gravity by appropriately breaking local conformal symmetry in matter kinetic and effective potential terms, without imposing an additional global symmetry?

sources.title: Dark energy from inspiraling in field space

evidence.text: Can a well-defined rotationally invariant two-field potential support long-lasting cosmic acceleration with persistently large turning, despite conservation of angular momentum in an expanding universe?

sources.title: Further Refining Swampland Conjecture on Inflation in General Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity

evidence.text: How does a phenomenological power-law correction modify nonminimally coupled quartic inflation and its potential-derivative constraints?

sources.title: Swampland conjectures in hybrid metric-Palatini gravity

evidence.text: The potential family tests whether changing the exponent away from the previously discussed quadratic case can improve simultaneous inflationary and swampland compatibility in the hybrid model.

sources.title: Swampland conjectures in hybrid metric-Palatini gravity

evidence.text: The hybrid action retains metric curvature R while adding f(𝓡), where 𝓡 is built from an independent connection. The construction supplies the modified gravitational dynamics used for the inflationary application.

sources.title: Swampland conjectures in hybrid metric-Palatini gravity

evidence.text: Does a power-law-potential realization of hybrid metric-Palatini inflation admit a common regime satisfying cosmological observations and the paper's de Sitter swampland inequalities? The proposed test uses ns, r, and potential-derivative ratios.

sources.title: Constraints on cosmological parameters in light of the scalar–tensor theory of gravity and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can power-law, exponential and logarithmic inflationary models in nonminimally coupled scalar–tensor gravity satisfy the paper's de Sitter swampland conditions while producing cosmological parameters compatible with its observational benchmarks?

sources.title: Swampland dS conjecture in mimetic $f(R, T)$ gravity

evidence.text: Can reconstructed inflationary histories in mimetic f(R,T)=R+δT gravity satisfy observational constraints and refined or further-refined de Sitter swampland criteria?

sources.title: Non-minimally coupled Natural Inflation: Palatini and Metric formalism with the recent BICEP/Keck

evidence.text: How does a polynomial nonminimal inflaton–curvature coupling change natural-inflation predictions for ns, r and α in Metric and Palatini formulations, and which sampled parameters agree with the BICEP/Keck contours used in this 2022 paper under specified reheating histories?

sources.title: Warm $\beta $-exponential inflation and the swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can temperature-cubic dissipation make β-exponential inflation end, agree with the quoted CMB constraints in weak or strong dissipation, and satisfy the paper’s three swampland tests?

sources.title: Further Refining Swampland dS Conjecture in Mimetic f(G) Gravity

evidence.text: Can a reconstructed slow-roll inflation model in mimetic f(G) gravity match the paper's observational benchmarks while satisfying the refined or further refined de Sitter swampland conjecture?

sources.title: Swampland Criteria and Constraints on Inflation in a $f(R,T)$ Gravity Theory

evidence.text: Can canonical-scalar inflation in the specified linear f(R,T) model satisfy the paper's Planck 2018 cuts together with its implementation of swampland criteria, and which potential parameters permit overlap?

sources.title: Kontsevich-Segal Criterion in the No-Boundary State Constrains Inflation

evidence.text: Does imposing the Kontsevich–Segal criterion on complex saddles of the semiclassical Hartle–Hawking no-boundary wave function select inflationary potentials and constrain the tensor-to-scalar ratio? What causes saddles to lose allowability during an approximately classical inflationary phase?

sources.title: Cosmic acceleration and turns in the Swampland

evidence.text: Does the Swampland Distance Conjecture (SDC), assumed valid with a positive scalar potential, permit rapid-turn multifield cosmic acceleration near infinite-distance boundaries, or constrain Ω/H?

sources.title: Theory of gravity with nonminimal matter-nonmetricity coupling and the de-Sitter swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can nonminimal matter–nonmetricity coupling reconcile single-scalar slow-roll inflation with the de Sitter swampland criteria?

sources.title: The de Sitter Swampland Conjectures in the Context of Chaplygin-Inspired Inflation

evidence.text: Can generalized Chaplygin-inspired single-field inflation satisfy the de Sitter swampland conditions, and how do these conditions further restrict inflationary potentials already constrained by CMB comparisons?

sources.title: The Standard Model Higgs boson as the inflaton

evidence.text: The analysis uses Einstein-frame potential slow-roll parameters, the e-fold integral and the COBE normalization U/ε=(0.027MP)⁴. The authors state that the same inflationary results can be obtained in the Jordan frame.

sources.title: Disentangling the $f(R)$ - Duality

evidence.text: Weyl transformation gives V=(f′R−f)/(2f′²). Reconstruction substitutes f′=exp(κφ), differentiates the resulting equation to solve for f′, and integrates; the original undifferentiated equation fixes the lost integration constant.

sources.title: Gauss-Bonnet Inflation

evidence.text: For f=λφ² in the Ricci-free model, the authors reduce the system to a Hubble evolution equation and integrate it for k=0. The relation φ²ȧ⁵=C0 is used to determine the scalar evolution, and a recursive Hubble-parameter hierarchy characterizes departure from inflation.

sources.title: Warm inflation within a supersymmetric distributed mass model

evidence.text: Weight the momentum-dependent on-shell rate by a Bose-Einstein distribution and normalize by number density. Factor out mass and coupling terms before approximating the remaining inverse-energy integral.

sources.title: $\alpha$-attractor from superconformal E-models in brane inflation

evidence.text: Numerical ns and r predictions are compared with the analytic approximations and scanned over α and V0/λ. Additional n values are examined. Later parameter plots use N=60 and the historical Planck 2018 and BICEP2/Keck constraints cited by the paper.

sources.title: A note on supergravity inflation in braneworld

evidence.text: Numerical slow-roll predictions use the modified e-fold integral N=−∫(YV/V′)dϕ, with Y=1+V/(2λ), and the scalar and tensor spectra appropriate to RSII. The authors report ending inflation at ε=1 because |η| is smaller at the exit point.

sources.title: How accidental was inflation?

evidence.text: How sensitively do supergravity inflation models depend on relative couplings, and can small departures from their Starobinsky or new-inflation limits improve CMB agreement while alleviating large-field initial-condition problems? The focus is potential-flatness tuning rather than the overall inflationary hierarchy.

sources.title: Higgs inflation and its extensions and the further refining dS swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Can metric Higgs inflation, Palatini Higgs inflation, and Higgs–Dilaton inflation satisfy the further-refined de Sitter conjecture through suitable choices of its parameters, despite reported tension with the earlier refined conjecture?

sources.title: Inflation models selected by the swampland distance conjecture with the Lyth bound

evidence.text: Can the swampland distance conjecture, combined with the Lyth bound and model-specific predictions, restrict representative large-field inflation models more strongly than the paper's quoted CMB constraints?

sources.title: Swampland conjecture and inflation model from brane perspective

evidence.text: Can an f(R) inflation model on a high-energy brane satisfy the paper’s swampland criteria and its observational comparisons simultaneously? The question concerns a proposed effective cosmological description; the paper does not construct its quantum-gravity completion.

sources.title: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term

evidence.text: How does scalar coupling to the Gauss–Bonnet term modify two-field rapid-turn inflation, its potential slow-roll relations and consistency conditions, and the possibility of phantom-like dark energy?

destination.title: Flux vacua, scale hierarchies and effective descriptions
destination.question: How do flux backgrounds and related effective theories realize lower-dimensional vacua, what controls their hierarchies, sources and spectra, and how can independently scoped consistency tests assess them?

sources.title: Supersymmetric AdS vacua and separation of scales

evidence.text: Do independently adjustable geometric parameters in supersymmetric massive-IIA AdS₄×S²(B₄) vacua permit scale separation after flux quantisation, and what can curvature ratios and a test-scalar KK spectrum establish?

sources.title: M-theory and Type IIA Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: What additional charge sources permit four-dimensional M-theory and conventional type IIA compactifications with internal four-form flux despite supergravity no-go constraints? The paper also assesses a specific massive-IIA proposal for parametrically separated AdS and Kaluza–Klein scales.

sources.title: AdS4 flux vacua in type II superstrings and their domain-wall solutions

evidence.text: Can perturbative type II compactifications produce supersymmetric AdS4 extrema with finite main moduli, and can their sources form domain walls connecting an AdS4 region to flat spacetime?

sources.title: A Second look at N=1 supersymmetric AdS(4) vacua of type IIA supergravity

evidence.text: Identify the ten-dimensional geometry behind a class of effective four-dimensional N=1 IIA AdS vacua, construct sources satisfying its RR two-form Bianchi identity, and exhibit a non-nearly-Kähler compactification within the same supersymmetry framework.

sources.title: On the Conformal Field Theory Duals of type IIA AdS(4) Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: What central-charge scaling, operator spectrum, symmetries, and approximate moduli-space geometry must a three-dimensional CFT dual to the studied type IIA AdS4 flux compactifications reproduce?

sources.title: The Effective theory of type IIA AdS(4) compactifications on nilmanifolds and cosets

evidence.text: What four-dimensional effective actions and light scalar spectra arise in the studied nilmanifold and coset AdS4 compactifications, and can geometric flux permit scale separation or evade the cited type IIA inflation no-go theorem?

sources.title: Type-IIA flux compactifications and N=4 gauged supergravities

evidence.text: How do geometric Type-IIA O6 flux compactifications map precisely to N = 4 gauging parameters and consistency constraints, and which previously known N = 1 AdS₄ vacua admit extended-supergravity embeddings?

sources.title: Heterotic compactifications on nearly Kahler manifolds

evidence.text: Can nearly Kähler heterotic AdS compactifications satisfy supersymmetry, anomaly cancellation, and the order-α′ equations of motion simultaneously, and how do the tangent-bundle connection and gaugino condensate affect existence and volume fixing?

sources.title: AdS vacua with scale separation from IIB supergravity

evidence.text: Can classical type IIB supergravity with O5/O7 sources produce supersymmetric AdS4 compactifications admitting weak coupling, large internal volume, and an AdS radius parametrically larger than the compactification scale?

sources.title: AdS$_{4}$ compactifications of AdS$_{7}$ solutions in type II supergravity

evidence.text: Can localized-source AdS7 solutions of massive IIA yield supersymmetric AdS4 compactifications through a twist over a compact three-manifold, and can the construction produce more general regular or sourced vacua?

sources.title: Remarks on scale separation in flux vacua

evidence.text: Can Maldacena–Nuñez-type restrictions on Minkowski and de Sitter flux vacua also obstruct AdS vacua whose KK masses are parametrically above the cosmological curvature scale? What would this imply for classical Romans-mass smoothing of O6 singularities?

sources.title: On scale separation in type II AdS flux vacua

evidence.text: Do apparent violations of AdS/KK scale separation and the strong AdS distance conjecture in selected type II flux EFTs survive when the internal geometry, its flux-dependent normalization, and the lightest KK directions are included?

sources.title: O‐Plane Backreaction and Scale Separation in Type IIA Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Does supersymmetry force a KK tower to track AdS curvature in every small-cosmological-constant limit? The paper tests this conjectural restriction using the localized continuation of DGKT vacua.

sources.title: O‐Plane Backreaction and Scale Separation in Type IIA Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Does the KK tower decouple from AdS curvature as the cosmological constant approaches zero? The diagnostic compares a squared KK mass with curvature, normalized consistently in the lower-dimensional theory.

sources.title: O‐Plane Backreaction and Scale Separation in Type IIA Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Does massive IIA O6-core resolution preserve the low-energy spectrum and hierarchy inferred from bulk supergravity? What next-order Kähler data and internal geometric structure describe the localized vacua?

sources.title: O‐Plane Backreaction and Scale Separation in Type IIA Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Which flux equations admit additional controlled scaling directions that change the KK/AdS hierarchy? Are orientifold sources necessary for such directions in string flux vacua?

sources.title: O‐Plane Backreaction and Scale Separation in Type IIA Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Can localized O6 sources preserve the controlled, stabilized, scale-separated AdS physics obtained from smeared type IIA Calabi-Yau orientifold solutions?

sources.title: O‐Plane Backreaction and Scale Separation in Type IIA Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Can localized codimension-three orientifold sources replace the uniform source densities used in DGKT flux vacua while retaining a controlled four-dimensional AdS effective theory?

sources.title: On supersymmetric AdS$_{4}$ orientifold vacua

evidence.text: Can supersymmetric massive-IIA backgrounds with localized orientifolds reproduce the defining integrated data of DGKT vacua? The aim is an initial ten-dimensional test of the proposal, motivated by its potential scale separation and tension with the Strong AdS Distance Conjecture.

sources.title: AdS$_{2}$ type-IIA solutions and scale separation

evidence.text: Can source-free type-IIA product backgrounds containing AdS2 exhibit parametrically separated compactification scales, and how do curvature bounds, Ricci-flat factors and flux quantization constrain that possibility?

sources.title: KKLT and the Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can an unconstrained flux parameter produce controlled AdS scale separation in a four-dimensional type IIA model?

sources.title: Smearing orientifolds in flux compactifications can be OK

evidence.text: Can massive IIA compactifications with localized O6 sources solve the ten-dimensional supergravity equations, and when does their smeared description approximate the localized fields? A second question concerns an exotic example whose unwarped internal boundary disappears after backreaction.

sources.title: Global properties of the conformal manifold for S-fold backgrounds

evidence.text: What are the ten-dimensional interpretation, global identifications and Kaluza–Klein consequences of the apparently noncompact modulus χ in a one-parameter family of N=2 AdS4 vacua?

sources.title: The holographic conformal manifold of 3d $ \mathcal{N} $ = 2 S-fold SCFTs

evidence.text: Can one construct a two-real-parameter family of N = 2 AdS4 J-fold vacua connecting known symmetry-enhanced solutions, and use holography to determine the corresponding conformal-manifold geometry and coupling-dependent operator spectrum?

sources.title: Leaps and bounds towards scale separation

evidence.text: What rigorous restrictions do higher-dimensional equations place on Kaluza–Klein masses and scale separation, and can Romans mass replace the problematic O6 loci in promising supersymmetric AdS4 compactifications by smooth local geometry?

sources.title: Non-supersymmetric AdS$_{6}$ and the swampland

evidence.text: Can the Kaluza-Klein scale become parametrically larger than the AdS6 curvature scale in these backgrounds?

sources.title: Comments on classical AdS flux vacua with scale separation

evidence.text: Do the scale-separated effective vacua survive localized orientifold backreaction and corrections beyond classical supergravity?

sources.title: Comments on classical AdS flux vacua with scale separation

evidence.text: Can internal excitations remain parametrically heavier than the AdS curvature scale while the compactification stays at weak coupling and large volume?

sources.title: Comments on classical AdS flux vacua with scale separation

evidence.text: Are the integer scalar dimensions of the original DGKT orbifold special to its simple volume polynomial and exchange symmetry?

sources.title: Integer conformal dimensions for type IIa flux vacua

evidence.text: Why do scalar operators dual to moduli in supersymmetric DGKT AdS4 flux vacua have integer, highly degenerate conformal dimensions, and does this universality extend to general Calabi–Yau orientifolds independently of fluxes and intersection numbers?

sources.title: AdS4 flux vacua in type II superstrings and their domain-wall solutions

evidence.text: Specify duality directions and transform bulk fields, sources and the effective Kähler/superpotential pair. In these constructions, transverse NS5 duality produces KK monopoles and geometric flux.

sources.title: A Second look at N=1 supersymmetric AdS(4) vacua of type IIA supergravity

evidence.text: Compute the Killing form of the geometric-flux algebra, change to two SU(2) invariant-form bases, and evaluate exterior derivatives of J and Ω to identify the intrinsic torsion classes and homogeneous metric.

sources.title: On the Conformal Field Theory Duals of type IIA AdS(4) Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Wrapped-brane supersymmetry is determined using κ-symmetry and calibration conditions. A separate DBI plus Wess–Zumino calculation gives the reported cancellation of radial forces for the displayed D4 configuration.

sources.title: The Effective theory of type IIA AdS(4) compactifications on nilmanifolds and cosets

evidence.text: Uses imported pure-spinor expressions for the superpotential and Kähler potential, with Mukai pairings, to construct the N=1 scalar potential. Physical scalar masses require diagonalizing the Hessian with the inverse scalar kinetic metric.

sources.title: Type-IIA flux compactifications and N=4 gauged supergravities

evidence.text: Generalized dimensional reduction of NSNS and RR vector field strengths is matched to standard N = 4 non-Abelian curvatures. This identifies flux-dependent generalized structure constants and thereby fixes the two-derivative gauged action.

sources.title: Heterotic compactifications on nearly Kahler manifolds

evidence.text: The equations are split into external and internal components. Factorized gaugino spinors obey a massless external Dirac equation, and assumed quantum averages of external bilinears supply a condensate source for the bosonic equations.

sources.title: Integer dual dimensions in scale-separated AdS$_{3}$ from massive IIA

evidence.text: Which massive-IIA G2-orientifold flux choices yield scale-separated supersymmetric AdS3 vacua with integer limiting dimensions for dual scalar operators, and can this behavior coexist with stabilization of all retained moduli?

membershipSample.placementReason: Covers quantized parameter families in the specified massive-IIA AdS compactification and the qualified use of curvature and test-scalar spectra to assess KK/AdS separation.
membershipSample.placementQualification: q0 covers the proposed controlled family, quantization constraint and partial spectral tests in this supersymmetric massive-IIA setting. It explicitly distinguishes curvature ratios from physical KK spectra. q2 supplies related methods, but q0 is more specific to the complete separation question. Neither the inherited surviving parameters nor the limited diagnostics settle the full KK gap or a no-go theorem.

destination.title: Conditional thermal Festina Lente constraints
destination.question: Under the stated equilibrium and near-ultracold discharge assumptions, what constraints follow from thermal pair creation and conduction by existing carriers?
destination.summary: Keeps the source's conjecture application separate from the underlying pair-production and conduction questions.

systems: An equilibrium bath containing charged carriers
regimes: Couplings within the stated conduction applicability domain
assumptions: Rapid discharge means losing an order-one charge fraction within a Hubble time
The collapse discussion uses homogeneous throat models
The conduction constraint does not rely on the computed photon-fusion rate
Phenomenological applications retain their additional model assumptions, including an unbroken sufficiently light B−L gauge sector where invoked
conventions: Keep c and g* explicit; c=1 and g*=2 are numerical benchmarks
Retain the stated logarithmic normalization sensitivity
Exponent-only criteria are comparisons rejected by this source, not accepted premises
includes: Source-announced neutrino, millicharge, effective-operator and inflationary applications
excludes: A model-independent bound for arbitrary black holes or nonequilibrium baths
Independent confirmation of present-day numerical exclusions

evidence.text: How do thermal pair creation and conduction by existing equilibrium charge carriers modify Nariai-black-hole discharge, the Festina Lente mass bound, and its particle-physics and inflationary implications?

destination.title: Counting and finiteness
destination.question: How many inequivalent vacua or vacuum-locus components occur under specified bounds, and when are exact counts, indices and continuum estimates reliable?
destination.summary: Keep the counted object, quotient, charge bound and boundary behavior explicit.

targets: Finiteness of vacua or connected components
assumptions: Global admissible-vacua finiteness is a different target from fixed-family finiteness.
conventions: Signed indices need not equal unsigned counts.
Finite connected components need not mean finitely many isolated points.
Minimum nonnegative and minimum strictly positive cosmological constant remain distinct.
excludes: Counting numerical endpoints as certified distinct vacua

sources.title: Finiteness of Flux Vacua from Geometric Transitions

evidence.text: What gauge-theory mechanism explains finiteness of supersymmetric flux vacua near local Calabi–Yau singularities, including conifold and Argyres–Douglas degenerations?

sources.title: R symmetries in the landscape

evidence.text: How severely does preserving a discrete R symmetry restrict flux choices in surveyed IIB compactifications, when do such configurations preserve supersymmetry classically, and how does their abundance differ from R-parity-preserving configurations?

sources.title: A Review of distributions on the string landscape

evidence.text: How can distributions in controllable string-vacuum ensembles guide phenomenological model building? How do finiteness, accumulation points and correlations among viable vacua affect predictivity?

sources.title: A Finite landscape?

evidence.text: Is the number of phenomenologically admissible four-dimensional string/M-theory vacua finite, despite potentially infinite choices of compactification topology, field configurations and fluxes?

sources.title: Applications of an exact counting formula in the Bousso-Polchinski Landscape

evidence.text: How can BP flux vacua be counted when the usual volume estimate fails, and what does improved counting imply for low-Λ abundances, typical flux occupation and estimates of the minimum nonnegative cosmological constant?

sources.title: Some Physical Consequences of an Exact Vacua Distribution in the Bousso-Polchinski Landscape

evidence.text: How can lattice vacua in very thin cosmological-constant shells be counted beyond the Bousso–Polchinski volume approximation, and what does the resulting distribution imply for flux occupation, the smallest positive cosmological constant and possible moduli-stabilization difficulties?

sources.title: Generalized Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Which supersymmetric vacua arise in the generalized-flux four-dimensional theory, can their coupling and cosmological constant be tuned, and does their apparent accumulation challenge landscape finiteness?

sources.title: Finiteness of volume of moduli spaces

evidence.text: Is the volume of a two-dimensional CFT moduli space finite in the Zamolodchikov metric, particularly after restricting to a region with a positive lower bound on nonzero operator dimensions? The motivation includes finiteness estimates for string vacua.

sources.title: On the taxonomy of flux vacua

evidence.text: Do explicit integral-flux solutions support the predicted curvature-dependent distribution of IIB no-scale vacua, and how does their number scale with the allowed flux D3 charge L?

sources.title: Counting flux vacua

evidence.text: How many duality-inequivalent supersymmetric flux vacua occur in type IIB Calabi–Yau compactification, how are they distributed, and under what conditions are their numbers finite and approximable by a signed geometric index?

sources.title: The Statistics of string / M theory vacua

evidence.text: Can estimates of the numbers and distributions of string/M vacua approximating the Standard Model clarify predictivity and falsifiability before identifying our vacuum?

sources.title: Lectures on constructing string vacua

evidence.text: How can approximate, controlled string vacua suitable for phenomenological model building be constructed and analyzed, especially IIB/F-theory flux compactifications with stabilized moduli, and what obstructs control?

sources.title: Flux vacua of the mirror octic

evidence.text: Can one explicitly enumerate all flux vacua at bounded flux number across the entire moduli space of a concrete type IIB orientifold, rather than sample fluxes or restrict to a boundary region?

sources.title: Finiteness theorems and counting conjectures for the flux landscape

evidence.text: For a fixed Calabi–Yau fourfold family and tadpole bound, are integral flux-vacuum loci finite in connected components, including near moduli-space boundaries? What further bounds govern their counting, complexity and dimension?

sources.title: Distributions of flux vacua

evidence.text: Determine counts and distributions of supersymmetric and nonsupersymmetric flux vacua over moduli, cosmological constant and supersymmetry-breaking parameters, including the validity of smooth approximations to quantized-flux counts.

sources.title: The String landscape and the swampland

evidence.text: Does the IIB complex coupling scalar have finite metric volume once physically equivalent configurations are identified? The example tests whether duality identifications are essential to the proposed scalar-volume restriction.

sources.title: On the explicit construction and statistics of Calabi-Yau flux vacua

evidence.text: Do explicit type IIB flux vacua in a two-complex-structure-modulus sector follow the Ashok–Douglas index density, and how do their locations, flux charges, axiodilaton values and supersymmetry-breaking scales distribute?

sources.title: Restrictions on infinite sequences of type IIB vacua

evidence.text: Can infinitely many distinct ISD flux vacua accumulate at degeneration limits, particularly the large-complex-structure point approached by previously reported vacuum sequences?

sources.title: On the geometry of moduli space of polarized Calabi-Yau manifolds

evidence.text: The physical motivation is a previously derived asymptotic flux-vacuum counting formula involving a Weil-Petersson curvature integral. Its finiteness implications retain caveats from the cited counting work.

sources.title: The Noether-Lefschetz problem and gauge-group-resolved landscapes: F-theory on K3  $\times$  K3 as a test case

evidence.text: How can F-theory flux vacua be counted while retaining gauge-group and other algebraic information, correctly identifying equivalent elliptic fibrations and relating discrete Noether–Lefschetz enumeration to continuous vacuum statistics?

sources.title: Comments on Brane Recombination, Finite Flux Vacua, and the Swampland

evidence.text: This orientifold patch provides a concrete setting in which negative orientifold charge, magnetized brane charge and positive flux charge must balance. Its explicit brane families make the assumptions behind finite-vacua counting accessible to scrutiny.

sources.title: Enumerating flux vacua with enhanced symmetries

evidence.text: How frequently do tree-level W=0 vacua and enhanced discrete symmetries occur in tractable IIB flux models, and how do their counts and moduli distributions depend on the D3-charge bound L?

destination.title: Controlled potentials and model construction
destination.question: Can inflationary potentials and exits be realized while controlling backreaction, loop effects, additional states and effective-theory validity?
destination.summary: Preserves potential flattening, protected hybrid construction, instanton hierarchies and positive-energy embeddings as separate model-building targets.

regimes: Model-specific effective theories, including a specified five-dimensional construction
assumptions: Flattening must be assessed after kinetic effects and stabilization are considered
States enforcing a conjecture need not dominate the inflationary potential
conventions: Use the relevant canonically normalized potential when a source requires it
excludes: Inferring eternal inflation from a viable finite-inflation potential

sources.title: Warped Hybrid Inflation

evidence.text: Can hybrid inflation combine a naturally flat PNGB inflaton potential with a rapid waterfall exit while avoiding excessive waterfall-loop corrections, using controlled five-dimensional effective field theory?

sources.title: Trans-Planckian Censorship and Inflation in Grand Unified Theories

evidence.text: Can the vacuum energy driving hybrid inflation be made much smaller than the underlying U(1)-breaking scale?

sources.title: Transplanckian axion monodromy!?

evidence.text: Can the spatial monodromy mechanism be embedded in a time-dependent positive-energy background suitable for inflation?

sources.title: Trans-Planckian Censorship and Inflation in Grand Unified Theories

evidence.text: What dynamics prepare the inflaton below the hilltop with a sufficiently small velocity, and what explains the tiny gauge coupling and flat potential?

sources.title: Fencing in the Swampland: Quantum Gravity Constraints on Large Field Inflation

evidence.text: Can weak-gravity-satisfying instantons be negligible during inflation? The setting separates the spectrum enforcing the full hull from terms dominating the inflaton potential.

sources.title: A potential mechanism for inflation from swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can integrating out states whose masses depend on an inflaton modulus flatten a steep geometric potential enough for slow roll while retaining the proposed quantum-gravity constraints?

sources.title: Tunnelling in Dante's Inferno

evidence.text: When can quantum tunnelling across the transverse potential barrier terminate inflation in Dante’s Inferno, and what additional restrictions follow from requiring its suppression during inflation?

sources.title: Simple exercises to flatten your potential

evidence.text: When does relaxation of heavy scalar fields in response to inflationary energy flatten the canonically normalized inflaton potential, and when do kinetic effects or loss of moduli stabilization prevent this mechanism?
